about: Merritt & Merritt Law Firm is a personal injury firm with six offices across Georgia, Florida and Texas.
The firm states that it works on a contingency fee, with nothing to pay unless the case is won; the first consultation is free; its intake line is open around the clock.

google.source: Google Business Profile via Places API. 6 listings, counts summed and rating weighted by count

completeness.note: Categories, opening hours, photo count and description come from the Places API. The services list, the Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the API does not expose at any price, so they are not scored either way.

G1.evidence: Georgia does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

G2.evidence: 2 of the firm's attorneys share a surname with a disciplined attorney, and for Debra Brown-Williams 1 of 1 decision(s) naming this surname have no searchable text, so they can be neither tied to nor ruled out against this attorney. The decisions that cannot be read are scans without searchable text, so this is a limit of the published record. Nothing here says the firm's attorney is that person.

G3.evidence: 6 physical locations verified on Google Business Profile. Georgia publishes no business register we can query for free. The Secretary of State sells the bulk corporations file over FTP, $500 for a single extract or $5,000 a year for weekly ones, and its free entity search answers an automated reader with a 403 on every path including its own robots file, which is a bot challenge we do not work around. A register that is for sale is a published record in the sense that matters here only if somebody buys it. This is a limit of the published record and not something the firm can change.

G5.evidence: Site has served over HTTPS, a working phone number published, 15 named attorneys published.
G5.source: Public crawl of the firm's own site

G6.evidence: 910 public client reviews across 6 Google listings, above the 10 minimum, and the firm's domain has been registered since 2012-11-17, so it has been operating for more than a year
G6.source: Google Places API and the domain's registration date over RDAP

operating.source: Domain registration date over RDAP, which is a lower bound on how long the firm has been operating rather than its founding date

accountability.evidence: no bar or trial lawyers' association named on the pages we read · no professional liability cover disclosed, which is not scored here: plaintiff firms in this market do not publish it, and an absence shared by every firm separates none of them

results_published.why: the site publishes no case-results page

score.verdict: 2 of 5 eligibility gates passed. 3 could not be answered from the available records (G1, G2, G3) and do not count against the firm. Strongest pillar: C; most headroom in pillar A (0/25).
